notes: Method: keywords-explorer-matching-terms, one deep phrase-match pass on the local word "esim" ordered by volume descending, one phrase-match pass on the competitor brands holafly, airalo, saily and ubigi, and one terms-match pass on the local phrase for "sim card abroad" or "sim card for travel". Metrics selected were keyword, volume, difficulty, cpc and parent_topic. Cost was a flat 23 units per returned row.

Every volume, difficulty and cpc in this file is a raw Ahrefs number copied from the API response. Nothing was estimated, interpolated or rounded. difficulty, cpc and parentTopic are null where Ahrefs itself returned null, usually on very recently discovered keywords. Volume is non-null on all 1089 rows, so no row is excluded from the totals for a missing volume.
Deduplication: every row was dropped whose (country, lowercased trimmed keyword) already appears in data/keyword-research.json. That removed 74 rows. No duplicates existed within this pass.

CONCENTRATION WARNING, read this before quoting the headline number. The new volume is heavily top-loaded. 32 bare competitor brand rows (holafly, airalo, saily, ubigi, nomad) carry 580250 searches a month, about 34 percent of the total, and they are navigational brand traffic, not a long tail we can win. 23 bare head rows (esim, karta esim, carte esim, tarjeta esim, esim karte, cartela esim and similar) carry another 357000, about 21 percent. The genuine long tail, meaning every row under 5000 searches a month, is 1030 keywords and 614160 searches a month. Treat 614160 as the realistic long-tail figure and the 1689510 total as the full addressable eSIM search surface in these eight markets.

Relevance filter, 370 rows dropped. Dropped: domestic mobile network and MVNO eSIM provisioning queries (aldi talk, congstar, o2, telekom, vodafone, otelo, klarmobil, lidl connect, blau, winsim, fraenk, freenet, callya in de; orange, sosh, free, bouygues, sfr, lycamobile, lebara, la poste mobile, nrj mobile, reglo mobile in fr; iliad, tim, vodafone, wind, windtre, fastweb, ho mobile, kena, coopvoce, postemobile, very mobile, optima in it; movistar, vodafone, orange, digi, lowi, simyo, yoigo, masmovil, jazztel, pepephone, euskaltel, finetwork in es; kpn, odido, simpel, simyo, youfone, hollandsnieuwe, ben, lyca, budget mobiel in nl; orange, play, plus, t-mobile, nju, plush in pl; meo, nos, digi, vodafone, uzo, woo, moche in pt; digi, orange, vodafone, telekom in ro). These are carrier support traffic, not travel demand. Also dropped: smartwatch, kids watch and Apple Watch eSIM queries, eSIM routers and eSIM adapters, and US carrier noise (lifewireless).

Kept deliberately despite carrying a carrier name: "orange travel esim", "vodafone travel esim" and "vodafone esim buitenland", because those are travel roaming products and therefore direct competitors.

Artifact filter, about 60 rows dropped. Ahrefs returned blocks of English-language brand boilerplate in non-English markets with round volumes and null difficulty, null cpc and null parent topic (for example "saily pricing" at 3200 in de and 3400 in fr, "saily alternatives", "saily official website", "werbeaktion saily" inside the nl index) plus LLM-prompt-shaped strings such as "what is the best esim for japan in france". These look like scraped or machine-generated index entries rather than real local demand, so they were excluded. If you want them counted, they would add roughly 60000 more searches a month, but I would not trust that number.

Home-market caveat. Terms like "esim portugal" (1900 in pt), "esim romania" (800 in ro), "esim espana" (2100 in es), "esim nederland" (1700 in nl), "esim polska" (600 in pl), "esim italia" (2300 in it), "esim france" (4000 in fr, kept) and "esim deutschland" (3700 in de) are classified as destination, but a meaningful share of that volume is locals looking for a domestic eSIM rather than inbound travellers. Do not plan inbound landing pages on those numbers without a SERP check.

The non-esim travel-connectivity head terms were almost empty everywhere. "sim karte ausland" returned 4 rows in de, "carte sim voyage" returned 2 in fr, "simkaart buitenland" returned 10 in nl, "karta sim za granica" returned 3 in pl, and the it, es, pt and ro equivalents returned zero rows above the volume floor. Non-eSIM travel SIM demand in Tier 1 Europe is effectively dead; the category has fully migrated to the word "esim".

Volume floors used, chosen to keep unit spend inside the cap: 150 for de, 50 for fr, it, es, nl and pl, 20 for pt and ro. Rows below those floors exist and were not measured, so the long tail in every market is deeper than what is in this file, in exchange for cheaper unit spend.

Row caps were also hit. The de, fr, it and es "esim" passes each returned the full requested limit (230, 190, 190, 190 rows), which means the list was truncated by the limit and not by the volume floor. There is more measurable long tail in those four markets at roughly 450 searches a month and below. nl, pl, pt and ro were not truncated.

Clusters were assigned by rule from multilingual token lists, not by hand, and intent was derived from the cluster (setup, device, generic and vs_alternatives are informational unless the keyword also contains a purchase verb, everything else commercial). Expect a small error rate on ambiguous rows.

Thin markets: ro-ro is genuinely small (74 new keywords, 23690 searches a month, and 23 of the 90 rows in the main pass came back with null difficulty and null cpc). pt-pt is also thin at 89 keywords and 52270 searches a month, and a large part of pt volume is Cabo Verde, Brazil and Morocco rather than classic European tourism.

Units: 38384 consumed by this agent, measured by summing the apiUsageCosts block returned with every call. The unitsRemaining figure is the whole workspace balance at the end of this pass and includes the parallel agent spend on other markets, so it is not attributable to this pass alone.
